headline: High-risk shared filesystem and server-side code execution make Dify↔Langflow prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystems and exchange content through uploaded files/server-side state, so one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted text. Dify’s shared datastore and Langflow’s server-side stores create a plausible bridge even without MCP or clipboard. This is not provably blocked, but the interaction is not inherently a raw-instruction channel, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify writes agent-generated text into a shared workspace or datastore that Langflow later reads as flow input
IF Langflow ingests uploaded or stored content from the same server-side state without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces or buckets
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files as instructions
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts
Require manual review before one agent consumes the other’s output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Langflow touches flow inputs and intermediate outputs; both have broad network egress and file access. In default deployments, either can upload or transmit sensitive content to model providers or HTTP services, so shared data can leak beyond the pair. The blast radius includes secrets and logs, making high appropriate.
conditions: IF either agent processes sensitive knowledge-base files, logs, or flow inputs
IF either agent sends those contents to configured model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data
Turn off external model/provider calls for the shared workflow
Use separate credentials and storage per agent
Redact logs and uploaded files before cross-agent transfer
requires-engineering: add DLP or content-classification gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and server-side Python execution, and both support multiple instances with shared server-side state. That creates a direct write-write conflict on the same mutable resources unless the operator adds locking or isolation. Because defaults are dangerous and corruption can be irreversible, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, datastore, or server-side store
IF concurrent runs modify shared files or state without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory
Serialize runs with a simple manual lock file
Disable concurrent writes to shared stores
Snapshot shared state before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform and Langflow chains multiple agents in graph flows, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input by design. Without an explicit verification step, errors or hallucinations from Dify can be propagated and operationalized by Langflow. That default trust chain can trigger incorrect downstream actions, so high fits.
conditions: IF Langflow consumes Dify-generated text as a flow node input
IF no validation or human review step is inserted between generation and action
mitigations: Insert a validation node between agents
Require human approval before any action-taking step
Constrain outputs to structured schemas
Log and compare outputs against source evidence
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or policy checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles knowledge base content and conversation logs, while Langflow handles flow inputs and intermediate outputs; both may retain sensitive data in server-side stores. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot claim a specific legal mismatch, but differing retention and logging practices can still create compliance exposure. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both agents
IF their retention, logging, or deletion behavior differs for that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems
Document retention and deletion settings for each agent
Use separate storage policies per agent
Review secret-handling paths before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
